{

    "test/users.test.js",
    "test/paginate.test.js",
    "test/server.test.js"
  ],
  "headline": "Intake mapped the API request, existing behavior, and decisions requiring discovery or recorded defaults.",
  "outcome": "done",
  "question_categories": [
    {"id": "K1", "applies": "yes"},

    {"id": "K10", "applies": "yes"},
    {"id": "K11", "applies": "yes"}
  ],
  "questions": [
    {
      "id": "Q1",
      "category": "K1",
      "question": "Who consumes the users API, and which existing clients or examples establish how they request and observe mutations and pages?",
      "changes": "Entry points, compatibility requirements, and boundary tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume HTTP clients use the existing server; no named client or separate interface is established.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the default proceeds; discovery should first identify clients and their current requests."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q2",
      "category": "K2",
      "question": "How can paginated listing be exposed while preserving existing endpoint responses, including the current unparameterized GET /users array?",
      "changes": "List endpoint compatibility, pagination interface, and regression tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Preserve existing unparameterized GET responses and consider explicit pagination parameters without changing the array response shape.",
      "blocks": "Final pagination contract; discovery must first establish existing clients and any documented pagination convention."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q3",
      "category": "K3",
      "question": "What are the create and delete request bodies, confirmation signal, status codes, errors, and response contents, and what does 'same shape' mean for each mutation?",
      "changes": "HTTP contract and boundary tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume POST /users and DELETE /users/:id, JSON inputs and outputs, an explicit per-request deletion confirmation, and array-shaped successful mutation responses matching the current list; exact fields and codes remain to be settled.",
      "blocks": "Final mutation contract; discovery must first inspect existing conventions and clients, then record defaults for details unsupported by evidence."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q4",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "What page size and validation rules apply to pages, user fields, duplicates, missing users, and deletion confirmation?",
      "changes": "Input validation, error behavior, and edge-case tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use positive 1-based pages, retain id/name/email records, reject malformed input and unconfirmed deletion, and choose a modest fixed page size if discovery finds no convention.",
      "blocks": "Final validation and page-size decisions; discovery must first look for client and project conventions."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q5",
      "category": "K4",
      "question": "Does the paginator handle a partially filled final page and empty or out-of-range pages as intended?",
      "changes": "Paginator correction and its boundary tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Treat the short last page as a defect: the current floor-based page count excludes it; preserve established behavior where compatible and verify the edge cases.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: source inspection establishes the short-page defect; later verification must exercise it."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q6",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "What Kestrel identifier format, allocation rules, uniqueness guarantees, and migration constraints must existing and new user IDs satisfy?",
      "changes": "ID generation, persisted data, migration compatibility, and tests.",
      "route": "research",
      "default": "Preserve existing numeric IDs and avoid reusing deleted IDs; do not claim Kestrel compatibility without evidence.",
      "blocks": "A verified migration-compatible ID design and completion claim; discovery must first locate the Kestrel migration specification or owner and establish access."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q7",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "What persistence location, initialization, failure handling, restart behavior, and concurrent-writer guarantees are expected?",
      "changes": "Storage design, data safety, configuration, and restart and concurrency tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Keep users in memory during operation, persist locally using built-in Node facilities, restore on restart, and assume one server process; preserve seeds on first initialization.",
      "blocks": "Final persistence contract; discovery must first establish deployment environment and any existing data-location or multi-process conventions."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q8",
      "category": "K5",
      "question": "How are actors identified, what user data is shared or hidden, and what state or confirmation persists across requests, devices, sessions, deletion, and restart?",
      "changes": "Authorization, privacy, confirmation lifecycle, and state tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Assume unauthenticated API clients share one process-wide user store, no actor identity or private per-user state is supplied, confirmation is explicit for each deletion request, and stored records persist until deleted; this does not provide per-actor access control or cross-process coordination.",
      "blocks": "Any claim of actor-specific authorization or privacy; discovery must first identify clients and runtime-provided identity or session facilities."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q9",
      "category": "K6",
      "question": "Are there environment-specific constraints on the storage path or runtime beyond Node 20 or later, zero dependencies, and the existing PORT override?",
      "changes": "Configuration and deployment compatibility.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use Node 20 or later, built-in modules only, and PORT with the existing fallback of 3000.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the default proceeds; discovery should first inspect available deployment configuration."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q10",
      "category": "K7",
      "question": "Which existing store, paginator, and server seams must remain callable independently by consumers or tests?",
      "changes": "Module boundaries and compatibility tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Retain independently testable user-store, paginator, and HTTP-server seams and preserve existing exports unless evidence requires otherwise.",
      "blocks": "Nothing: the default proceeds; discovery should first inspect imports and current tests."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q11",
      "category": "K8",
      "question": "Which boundary checks demonstrate creation, cautious deletion, pagination including a short last page, unchanged existing responses, and survival across a restart?",
      "changes": "Verification coverage and completion evidence.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Use the existing node:test framework through npm test, with HTTP-boundary checks and isolated persistence/restart checks.",
      "blocks": "Completion verification; discovery must first establish the final contracts and a safe temporary storage arrangement."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q12",
      "category": "K9",
      "question": "Is there a named deployment target or delivery access beyond the requested project checkout?",
      "changes": "Delivery location, access requirements, and release steps.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Deliver the result in this project checkout; no external deployment target or release authority is established.",
      "blocks": "External deployment, if one is later identified; discovery must first locate target and access evidence."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q13",
      "category": "K10",
      "question": "Are there established limits for request size, user data exposure, or deletion safeguards that this API must meet?",
      "changes": "Security and resource limits and their tests.",
      "route": "inspect",
      "default": "Keep the API simple, reject malformed input and unconfirmed deletion, and avoid assuming authentication or a specific performance target.",
      "blocks": "Claims of additional security or performance guarantees; discovery must first inspect project and deployment conventions."
    },
    {
      "id": "Q14",
      "category": "K11",
      "question": "Which evidence can resolve the risks of incompatible Kestrel IDs, accidental deletion, persistence loss, and a pagination response change early?",
      "changes": "Acceptance criteria, risk-focused checks, and delivery readiness.",
      "route": "research",
      "default": "Prioritize migration specification discovery and focused contract, deletion, restart, and pagination checks; keep unresolved migration compatibility visible.",
      "blocks": "A verified completion claim for any unresolved risk; discovery must first locate migration sources and establish the API and storage contracts."
    }
  ],
  "summary": "S1 [fact] The target is the Node users API in this folder; this intake is read-only, starts no server, makes no changes, and grants no external delivery authority. S2 [outcome] HTTP consumers need user creation and deliberately confirmed deletion; discovery or the recorded defaults in Q1, Q3, Q4, and Q8 settle the contract and safeguards before their final design. S3 [outcome and fact] Add listing pagination using the existing paginator and verify the short last page; its current floor-based page count drops that page, while Q2 and Q4 resolve compatibility and page size. S4 [boundary] Keep the implementation simple and dependency-free, using the existing Node runtime and built-in facilities. S5 [outcome] Retain the in-memory store while making users survive restarts; Q7 and Q8 cover ownership, lifetime, visibility, concurrency, and runtime-provided state. S6 [boundary] A later delivery run must fan out handler and test work, run improve until it stops finding issues, and perform code review before completion; this intake performs none of that work. S7 [outcome and risk] Preserve IDs for the next-quarter Kestrel migration; discovery must establish its actual identifier contract before compatibility can be claimed, with Kestrel migration documents, the migration team or owner, relevant workspace channels, internal sites, and private repositories as unverified leads; no specific locator or owner is known, and sensitive locators belong only in an authorized private store, never KNOWLEDGE/. S8 [fact] The existing usual port is 3000 with a PORT override. S9 [open contract] The current list returns a JSON array of user objects; discovery or Q3's recorded default must settle how mutation responses use that shape. S10 [boundary] Preserve existing endpoint responses, including GET /users and GET /users/:id, while Q2 resolves how pagination is requested; the intended result becomes usable in this project checkout after the later delivery run returns, an isolated source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return, and any deployed outcome exists only after a separately authorized release."
}

commands.command: /bin/zsh -lc 'for f in AGENTS.md ../AGENTS.md ../../AGENTS.md; do if [ -f "$f" ]; then cat "$f"; fi; done'
